test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is a ‘bawri’?

options.text: A traditional way of collecting water
An underground tank to store water
A canal providing water to agricultural land

solution:
The correct answer is __**A traditional way of collecting water.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **'bawri'** is a traditional way of **collecting water.**
 
• It is a stepwell, which is a type of well or pond that was used for** accessing groundwater** in ancient times.
 
• Stepwells were constructed by **digging into the ground **and building steps leading down to the water level.
 
• They were commonly found in the **arid regions of India** and were used for both **irrigation and drinking **water.
 
• Stepwells were also used for **social gatherings and religious** ceremonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **narrow bore tube-well** is a modern method of accessing groundwater.

 
 
• It involves** drilling a narrow borehole** into the ground and installing a tube or pipe to bring the water to the surface.
 
• This method is commonly used in areas where groundwater is available at a **deep level.**
 
 
 
• An **underground tank** is a storage facility for water.
 
 
• It is used to store water for **later use,** particularly in areas where water is scarce.
 
 
 
• A** canal **is a man-made waterway that is used to** transport water** from one place to another.
 
 
• Canals are commonly used for** irrigation,** particularly in agricultural areas.
